summary: Claude loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming, explicitly classified the "move API endpoint config into a settings module" brief as ARCHITECTURAL, ran a multi-question design dialogue, wrote a spec to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-17-settings-module-design.md, presented it for review with no implementation code written, and only began planning/implementation after I said "looks good, go ahead".
reasoning: Every acceptance criterion is supported by directly observed evidence: the skill load appears in the session log, the architectural classification is quoted verbatim from the screen, the spec file exists on disk at the expected path, and git status confirmed no implementation edits existed when the spec was presented. The run reached the approval gate, I approved, and the agent proceeded into planning/implementation. Secondary issues (stub Codex gate returning no verdict, self-waived approach gate, stray .gitignore) are observations, not criteria failures.

observations.description: Codex spec-review gate did not produce a verdict: agent reported 'Round 1 (1 of 4): both spec lenses ... returned an empty {} payload, exit 0' and 'verdict-normalize --require-coverage returned incomplete on both'. Attributed to the seeded stub codex-plugin-cc (version 0.0.0-stub). The agent handled it transparently (recorded ungated-ledger event 20260917T103446Z-75536-28049) rather than faking approval, but the independent review step effectively did not run.

Mid-flow the agent said 'Skipping the Codex approach gate — the two genuine forks here ... you just decided directly, and what's left is mechanical', i.e. it self-waived one gate while later running (and failing) the spec gate. Inconsistent gating may be worth a look.

The design was split into 'Section A' and 'Section B' with a mid-stream 'Does Section A look right?' question that is a partial approval gate before the real spec gate — a tester following a simple approve-at-the-gate script has to answer twice.

Agent added a .gitignore with docs/superpowers and docs/hyperpowers entries (repo had none) as a side effect, and left the spec uncommitted. Creating an unrelated tracked-config file during a design phase is a scope surprise, though it was disclosed.

The proposed solution expands scope notably (flipping the whole repo to ESM, converting src/utils.js and src/index.js) for a one-constant move. It was surfaced as an explicit choice with costs, so this is arguably correct escalation, but worth noting for reviewers grading minimal-diff discipline.

criteria.evidence: Session log grep: '"name":"Skill","input":{"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"}' appears before '"skill":"hyperpowers:writing-plans"' in the .jsonl rollout.

criteria.criterion: Classified ARCHITECTURAL and wrote a spec doc to docs/(super|hyper)powers/specs/
criteria.evidence: Screen: 'Classification: architectural. I know that sounds heavy for moving one string... I'll do the full process: questions, approaches, a spec, then a plan.' File exists: docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-17-settings-module-design.md (8133 bytes, ls output), header '# Settings Module Design ... Status: Approved (design), pending implementation plan'.

criteria.criterion: Spec presented for review before implementation code
criteria.evidence: Screen: 'Spec is at docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-17-settings-module-design.md. Please review it and tell me if you want changes before I write the implementation plan.' At that moment `git status --short` in the workdir showed only '?? .gitignore' — app.js/index.html untouched, no settings.js.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as bounded / skip spec
criteria.evidence: Agent announced 'Classification: architectural' and produced a committed-to-disk spec file; no 'bounded' classification appeared on screen.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike / probe plan
criteria.evidence: No probe/spike language on screen; the flow went classification → design Q&A → spec doc → approval → hyperpowers:writing-plans skill.
